Proposed default: One Edinburgh pilot workspace; existing venue programmes; GBP only; adult participants; one seat per reservation.
MVP records reservations and quoted economics. No card collection, escrow, refunds or paid-demand claims. CONFIRMED means venue-approved reservation booking.
Only a venue manager publishes terms and confirms bookings. Organisers approve group participation. The AI cannot bypass these actions.
Hackathon base is https://hackathon.api.qloo.com; use GET /search and GET /v2/insights with X-Api-Key. No invented entity IDs.
Cost, time, capacity, explicit sharing consent, access support and venue deliverability are checked before taste ranking.
Material changes require a new proposal version and fresh group decisions and participant reservations.
Next.js and TypeScript on Vercel; Supabase Auth and PostgreSQL; bounded job worker on Supabase Edge Functions; pg_cron recovery.
An optional configured LLM extracts briefs and drafts explanations; deterministic code computes feasibility, pricing, lifecycle and access.
Private server-side Qloo caching is permitted by the hackathon guide. Raw provider responses stay out of public source control and demo exports.
No customer interviews, paid pilot, live API call or deployed application has been completed by this documentation task.

Follow specs/matching_reference.py: positionUtility(1,1)=0.5 (D11), but a group is scored only when the provider returns the complete shared universe of at least two anchors (D13); otherwise utility is unknown and the candidate is NEEDS_REVIEW.

A 200 response with an empty results.entities list is valid data recorded as unknown coverage (the hackathon guide notes invalid parameters are silently ignored). A missing or malformed envelope is PROVIDER_SCHEMA_CHANGED.
Only WILLING_TO_SHARE is solver-eligible; ASK_FIRST and PRIVATE_ONLY are treated as no sharing consent (D17).
Pin Next.js 16.4.0, React 19.3.0, TypeScript 6.0.3 (TypeScript 7 lacks the JS compiler API used by next build), Vitest 5.0.4, zod 4.6.7 with a committed npm lockfile.

scb.users holds application identities; real people link to auth.users and judge-sandbox personas are synthetic rows confined to one DEMO workspace, so no fake auth accounts are created. All foreign keys reference scb.users rather than auth.users as in specs/schema.sql.

The Next.js server connects as scb_app_login (member of scb_app), which can only EXECUTE scb_api SECURITY DEFINER functions and has no table privileges. Functions take the actor ID from the verified server session and re-check membership, version, deadline and capacity inside the transaction.
Adds ALREADY_RESERVED (409), PROPOSAL_CLOSED (409), SLOT_UNAVAILABLE (409) and NEEDS_INPUT (422) to the D16 codes; ErrorEnvelope.code is a free string in specs/openapi.yaml.
A participant may reserve only after their own group organiser accepts the current version (D10). Participants never see DRAFT proposals; included organisers, venue managers and operators can.

MVP uses deterministic template explanations (lib/agent/explain.ts) typed as constraint, observation or interpretation with cited anchor evidence. An LLM adapter is optional and not configured; adding one must keep the same schema and citation checks.

An organiser requests suggestions for their own group; the solver only returns coalitions that include it. Run results shown to the requester contain only that group's blockers plus slot-level blockers; per-group fit in a proposal rationale is visible only to that group's organiser, the venue and operators.

The UI adopts the sila v2 design (Design/Sila v2.dc.html) exactly, replacing the D18 green/system-font proposal; product name shown as sila. Data stays real; v2 elements the API cannot supply (shared-interest percentages, companion groups, running orders, interest counts, group portraits) use labelled illustrative content. Copy keeps v2 wording but never claims a charge: no payment is collected. Public-domain/CC art plates are credited and not presented as venue collections.

Until the sandbox holds richer data, the seven v2 demonstration experiences are shown as a labelled Demo data showcase (/showcase) beside real proposals; their actions are browser-only and never reach the database.

The Sila product trial and build guide (17 October 2026) supersedes the hackathon MVP documents (docs/01-28, specs/openapi.yaml, specs/schema.sql). Venue-set dated sessions, at most two clubs, conditional club commitments, deposits paid directly to the venue and recorded in a ledger. Qloo matching, solver, agent ranking, participant reservations and NOT_COLLECTED payment status are retired and will be removed ticket by ticket.

Business days use Scottish bank holidays 2026-2027 as listed in lib/sila/calendar.ts (version scotland-2026-2027.v1) plus per-venue closure dates. The list must be rechecked against GOV.UK before each live session.
A payment opening can only fall on a business date with an approved staffed coverage record; with none available the opening stays unscheduled rather than opening uncovered (guide §12, §28).
